item.title: Reference-Guided Mesh Coloring with Blender MCP
item.description: A comprehensive architectural blueprint for extending blender-mcp-bridge to automatically ingest untextured STL models, align reference photos, execute semantic face selection, and project colors/textures onto 3D geometry using AI vision-in-the-loop workflows.

item.title: From Brackets to Enclosures
item.description: A Raspberry Pi 5 snap-fit enclosure puts blender-mcp-bridge through a more demanding agentic test. Claude and Codex successfully construct and verify base-and-lid geometry, while Google Antigravity takes a different path and generates Blender Python instead. The experiment highlights an important distinction: MCP provides the modeling capabilities, but each agent decides how to use them.

item.title: Bridging Digital and Physical Worlds
item.description: An exploration of the boundary between digital and physical fabrication. From first 3D prints to AI-driven Blender automation, this post examines how state management, deterministic workflows, bidirectional synchronization, and feedback loops shape reliable systems across both software and hardware.

item.title: Blender MCP for n8n
item.description: Blender MCP for n8n is a Model Context Protocol (MCP) bridge that allows n8n AI workflows to directly control Blender’s Python API. The system combines a Blender addon, a stateless/stateful MCP bridge server, and a record-and-replay session framework to enable deterministic, reproducible 3D scene generation from natural language. With 70+ structured tools spanning modeling, materials, animation, architectural workflows, and MEP systems, complex scenes can be constructed, tested, and replayed reliably through AI-directed tool calls.

item.title: AI-Driven 3D Workflows with n8n
item.description: This post explores how to integrate n8n, OpenRouter, and Blender MCP to create AI-driven 3D modeling workflows. Starting with an AI agent chat in n8n, I bridge prompts to Blender using a custom server, generating a condominium prototype complete with materials, landscaping, and cinematic lighting. Along the way, I highlight practical challenges—like material tuning and lighting setup—and show how automation and AI make complex 3D tasks conversational and modular. The result is a workflow that moves closer to a no-code, AI-powered approach to 3D design.

item.title: Blender Meets MCP
item.description: A step-by-step guide to integrating the Model Context Protocol (MCP) with Blender. From setup and server connections to building a datacenter model, discover how AI-driven workflows enhance 3D design and creativity.
